nodes.label: Tops
nodes.description: Anything worn on the upper half of the body, from a plain t-shirt to a knitted sweater.

nodes.label: Bottoms
nodes.description: Anything worn on the lower half of the body, such as trousers, jeans, shorts or a skirt.

nodes.label: Outerwear
nodes.description: The layer worn over everything else to keep warm or dry, such as a coat, jacket or blazer.

nodes.label: Dresses and one-piece garments
nodes.description: Garments that cover the top and bottom of the body in a single piece, such as a dress, a jumpsuit or a suit.

nodes.label: Shoes and footwear
nodes.description: Whatever is worn on the feet, from trainers to heels to boots.

nodes.label: Accessories
nodes.description: Smaller worn items that finish an outfit, such as hats, bags, glasses, belts and jewellery.

nodes.label: Materials and fabrics
nodes.description: What the clothing is actually made of, because the same shape in denim and in silk reads completely differently.

nodes.label: Fit and silhouette
nodes.description: How the clothing sits on the body — loose, tight, boxy, cropped — which changes the whole shape of a shot.

nodes.label: Clothing styles
nodes.description: The overall fashion language of an outfit, such as streetwear, office wear or vintage.

nodes.label: T-shirt
nodes.description: A simple short-sleeved top with no buttons and no collar, the most ordinary upper garment there is.

nodes.label: Graphic t-shirt
nodes.description: A t-shirt with a printed image, logo or slogan across the front.

nodes.label: Long-sleeve top
nodes.description: A close-fitting knit top with sleeves that reach the wrists.

nodes.label: Button-up shirt
nodes.description: A collared top that fastens down the front with buttons, from a crisp office shirt to a loose casual one.

nodes.label: Oxford shirt
nodes.description: A neat cotton button-up shirt with a soft collar, the standard smart-but-simple shirt.

nodes.label: Flannel shirt
nodes.description: A soft brushed-cotton button-up shirt, usually in a checked or plaid pattern, often worn open over a tee.

nodes.label: Denim shirt
nodes.description: A button-up shirt cut from denim, heavier and more rugged than a normal shirt.

nodes.label: Blouse
nodes.description: A softer, more flowing shirt-like top, usually in a fine fabric and often without a stiff collar.

nodes.label: Knit sweater
nodes.description: A warm knitted top pulled on over the head, what British English calls a jumper.

nodes.label: Cable-knit sweater
nodes.description: A thick sweater with raised rope-like braids twisting down the front.

nodes.label: Hoodie
nodes.description: A thick cotton sweatshirt with a hood attached, usually with a front pocket.
examples: an oversized grey hoodie with the hood down

nodes.label: Zip-up hoodie
nodes.description: A hoodie that opens all the way down the front with a zip instead of pulling over the head.

nodes.label: Sweatshirt
nodes.description: A thick soft cotton top with long sleeves and a round neck, like a hoodie without the hood.

nodes.label: Crop top
nodes.description: A top cut short so it ends above the waist and leaves the midriff visible.

nodes.label: Tank top
nodes.description: A sleeveless top with shoulder straps and no collar.

nodes.label: Camisole
nodes.description: A light sleeveless top on thin straps, usually in a smooth fabric like satin.

nodes.label: Turtleneck
nodes.description: A knitted top whose collar rolls right up around the neck.

nodes.label: Mock-neck top
nodes.description: A top with a short standing collar that covers the base of the neck but does not fold over.

nodes.label: Polo shirt
nodes.description: A knit top with a small collar and two or three buttons at the throat.

nodes.label: Bodysuit
nodes.description: A close-fitting top that continues between the legs so it never untucks.

nodes.label: Corset top
nodes.description: A stiffened, tightly shaped top with visible boning or lacing that cinches the waist.

nodes.label: Halter top
nodes.description: A sleeveless top held up by a strap that goes around the back of the neck, leaving the shoulders and back bare.

nodes.label: Off-shoulder top
nodes.description: A top whose neckline sits below the shoulders so both shoulders are bare.

nodes.label: Sports jersey
nodes.description: A team sports shirt, usually in breathable mesh with a number or team name on it.

nodes.label: Cardigan
nodes.description: A knitted top that opens all the way down the front with buttons, worn as a light extra layer.

nodes.label: Sweater vest
nodes.description: A sleeveless knitted layer worn over a shirt.

nodes.label: Trousers
nodes.description: Full-length legwear with a separate leg for each leg, called pants in American English.

nodes.label: Tailored trousers
nodes.description: Sharply cut trousers with a pressed crease down the front, the kind worn with a suit.

nodes.label: Jeans
nodes.description: Trousers made from denim, the everyday hard-wearing blue cotton fabric.
examples: faded blue jeans with a worn hem

nodes.label: Wide-leg jeans
nodes.description: Jeans cut loose and straight or flaring from the hip down, so the leg hangs wide over the shoe.

nodes.label: Skinny jeans
nodes.description: Jeans cut close to the leg all the way down to a narrow ankle.

nodes.label: Cargo trousers
nodes.description: Loose trousers with big patch pockets on the thighs.

nodes.label: Chinos
nodes.description: Plain cotton trousers, smarter than jeans but softer than suit trousers.

nodes.label: Track pants
nodes.description: Light sporty trousers with an elastic waist, usually with a stripe down the side.

nodes.label: Sweatpants
nodes.description: Thick soft cotton trousers with an elastic waist and cuffs, made for comfort.

nodes.label: Leggings
nodes.description: Very stretchy trousers that cling to the leg, usually worn for exercise or as a base layer.

nodes.label: Shorts
nodes.description: Legwear that stops somewhere between the upper thigh and the knee.

nodes.label: Denim shorts
nodes.description: Shorts cut from denim, often with a raw frayed hem.

nodes.label: Skirt
nodes.description: A garment that hangs from the waist as one open piece instead of having separate legs.

nodes.label: Mini skirt
nodes.description: A short skirt that ends well above the knee.

nodes.label: Midi skirt
nodes.description: A skirt that ends around mid-calf, between a mini and a full-length one.

nodes.label: Maxi skirt
nodes.description: A long skirt that falls to the ankle or the floor.

nodes.label: Pleated skirt
nodes.description: A skirt folded into sharp regular pleats that fan out as the wearer moves.

nodes.label: Culottes
nodes.description: Very wide cropped trousers cut so loosely that they look like a skirt.

nodes.label: Leather trousers
nodes.description: Trousers cut from leather or a leather-look material, with a glossy surface that catches light.

nodes.label: Trench coat
nodes.description: A long belted coat with a double-breasted front, originally made for rain.
examples: a beige trench coat left open over a dark outfit

nodes.label: Leather jacket
nodes.description: A short jacket made of leather, usually cut close to the body.

nodes.label: Biker jacket
nodes.description: A leather jacket with a slanted zip, wide lapels and studs or buckles, the classic motorcycle shape.

nodes.label: Denim jacket
nodes.description: A short button-up jacket made of denim.

nodes.label: Puffer jacket
nodes.description: A thick padded jacket quilted into horizontal tubes, made for cold weather.

nodes.label: Blazer
nodes.description: A structured tailored jacket with lapels, worn over a shirt for a smart look.

nodes.label: Parka
nodes.description: A long warm hooded coat built for real cold, often with fur trim around the hood.

nodes.label: Bomber jacket
nodes.description: A short jacket with a zip front and elastic cuffs and hem, based on a pilot's jacket.

nodes.label: Wool overcoat
nodes.description: A long formal coat cut from thick wool, worn over a suit or a knit.

nodes.label: Peacoat
nodes.description: A short double-breasted wool coat with broad lapels, originally worn by sailors.

nodes.label: Windbreaker
nodes.description: A thin unlined jacket in slippery synthetic fabric that blocks wind.

nodes.label: Raincoat
nodes.description: A waterproof coat that keeps rain out, often with a shiny surface.

nodes.label: Varsity jacket
nodes.description: A wool jacket with leather sleeves and a big letter or logo on the chest, the American school-team jacket.

nodes.label: Shearling jacket
nodes.description: A heavy leather jacket lined with woolly fleece that shows at the collar and cuffs.

nodes.label: Gilet
nodes.description: A sleeveless padded jacket that warms the body but leaves the arms free.

nodes.label: Anorak
nodes.description: A hooded shell jacket that pulls over the head instead of opening fully at the front.

nodes.label: Cape
nodes.description: A sleeveless layer that drapes from the shoulders over the arms.

nodes.label: Robe
nodes.description: A long loose layer that wraps across the front and ties at the waist.

nodes.label: Layered coat over a jacket
nodes.description: Two outer layers worn at once, such as a coat over a blazer, which reads as a deliberate styling choice rather than one garment.
nodes.prompt_fragment: a coat layered over a jacket

nodes.label: Dress
nodes.description: A single garment covering the body from the shoulders down past the hips, worn instead of a separate top and bottom.

nodes.label: Slip dress
nodes.description: A thin strappy dress cut like an undergarment, usually in a smooth fluid fabric.

nodes.label: Shirt dress
nodes.description: A dress cut like a long button-up shirt, with a collar and buttons down the front.

nodes.label: Wrap dress
nodes.description: A dress that crosses over at the front and ties at the waist rather than fastening with buttons.

nodes.label: Knit dress
nodes.description: A dress made from soft knitted fabric that follows the body.

nodes.label: Sundress
nodes.description: A light sleeveless dress in thin fabric, made for hot weather.

nodes.label: Evening gown
nodes.description: A long formal dress that reaches the floor, worn to grand occasions.

nodes.label: Jumpsuit
nodes.description: A one-piece garment that joins a top and full-length trousers.

nodes.label: Romper
nodes.description: A one-piece garment that joins a top and shorts, like a short jumpsuit.

nodes.label: Dungarees
nodes.description: Trousers with a bib front held up by two shoulder straps.

nodes.label: Suit
nodes.description: A matching jacket and trousers or skirt cut from the same fabric, worn as one outfit.

nodes.label: Tracksuit
nodes.description: A matching sporty jacket and trousers worn as a set.

nodes.label: Sneakers
nodes.description: Soft lace-up shoes with a rubber sole, called trainers in British English.

nodes.label: Chunky sneakers
nodes.description: Trainers with an exaggerated thick sole that adds visible height and bulk.

nodes.label: Running shoes
nodes.description: Light technical trainers built for running, with a cushioned sole and mesh upper.

nodes.label: Boots
nodes.description: Footwear that rises above the ankle.

nodes.label: Combat boots
nodes.description: Heavy lace-up boots with a thick tread, based on military footwear.

nodes.label: Chelsea boots
nodes.description: Neat ankle boots with a stretchy elastic panel at the side and no laces.

nodes.label: Knee-high boots
nodes.description: Boots whose shafts rise all the way up to or past the knee.

nodes.label: Cowboy boots
nodes.description: Pointed boots with a slanted heel and decorative stitching, from western dress.

nodes.label: Loafers
nodes.description: Flat slip-on leather shoes with no laces.

nodes.label: Oxford shoes
nodes.description: Smart laced leather shoes worn with a suit.

nodes.label: High heels
nodes.description: Shoes with a raised heel that tips the foot forward and lengthens the leg.

nodes.label: Stiletto heels
nodes.description: Heels with a very thin, very tall spike.

nodes.label: Block heels
nodes.description: Heels with a wide square column instead of a thin spike, so they look sturdier.

nodes.label: Sandals
nodes.description: Open shoes held on by straps, leaving most of the foot bare.

nodes.label: Flip-flops
nodes.description: The simplest sandal, a flat sole held on by a V-shaped strap between the toes.

nodes.label: Ballet flats
nodes.description: Very flat soft shoes with a low-cut front, shaped like a ballet slipper.

nodes.label: Mary Janes
nodes.description: Rounded flat or low-heeled shoes with a strap across the top of the foot.

nodes.label: Mules
nodes.description: Shoes with no back, so the heel of the foot is uncovered.

nodes.label: Platform shoes
nodes.description: Shoes with a thick slab of sole under the whole foot, adding height everywhere rather than just at the heel.

nodes.label: Barefoot
nodes.description: No footwear at all, which is a deliberate styling choice rather than a missing detail.

nodes.label: Headwear
nodes.description: Anything worn on the head, from a baseball cap to a wide-brimmed hat.

nodes.label: Baseball cap
nodes.description: A soft cap with a curved peak at the front.

nodes.label: Beanie
nodes.description: A soft knitted hat that hugs the head, worn for warmth.

nodes.label: Bucket hat
nodes.description: A soft round hat with a short brim that slopes down all the way around.

nodes.label: Wide-brim hat
nodes.description: A hat with a broad brim circling the head, which shades the face and casts a strong shadow.

nodes.label: Beret
nodes.description: A soft flat round hat with no brim, tilted on the head.

nodes.label: Fedora
nodes.description: A structured felt hat with a pinched crown and a medium brim.

nodes.label: Headscarf
nodes.description: A square of cloth tied over or around the hair.

nodes.label: Hood up
nodes.description: The hood of a hoodie or coat pulled up over the head, which frames and shadows the face.

nodes.label: Sunglasses
nodes.description: Tinted glasses that hide the eyes and read as instant attitude in a portrait.

nodes.label: Eyeglasses
nodes.description: Clear prescription glasses worn on the face.

nodes.label: Scarf
nodes.description: A long piece of fabric wrapped around the neck for warmth or decoration.

nodes.label: Gloves
nodes.description: Coverings for the hands, with separate fingers.

nodes.label: Belt
nodes.description: A strap around the waist, which both holds up trousers and marks the waistline in a silhouette.

nodes.label: Necktie
nodes.description: A long strip of fabric knotted at the collar and hanging down the shirt front.

nodes.label: Bow tie
nodes.description: A small ribbon tied into a bow at the collar, worn for formal occasions.

nodes.label: Backpack
nodes.description: A bag carried on the back by two shoulder straps.

nodes.label: Shoulder bag
nodes.description: A bag hung from one shoulder by a single strap.

nodes.label: Tote bag
nodes.description: A large open-topped bag carried by two short handles.

nodes.label: Crossbody bag
nodes.description: A small bag worn on a long strap that crosses the chest.

nodes.label: Necklace
nodes.description: A chain or cord worn around the neck, sometimes with a pendant.

nodes.label: Earrings
nodes.description: Jewellery worn on the ears, from small studs to large hoops.

nodes.label: Rings
nodes.description: Jewellery worn on the fingers, often several at once.

nodes.label: Bracelet
nodes.description: Jewellery worn around the wrist.

nodes.label: Wristwatch
nodes.description: A watch worn on the wrist.

nodes.label: Socks
nodes.description: Soft coverings for the feet worn inside shoes, sometimes deliberately pulled up so they show.

nodes.label: Tights
nodes.description: Close-fitting legwear covering the legs and hips, worn under skirts and dresses.

nodes.label: Face mask
nodes.description: A covering worn over the nose and mouth, which hides most of the face in a portrait.

nodes.label: Headphones
nodes.description: Over-ear headphones worn on the head, which read as an outfit element in street photography.

nodes.label: Hair ribbon
nodes.description: A ribbon or fabric bow tied into the hair.
nodes.prompt_fragment: a ribbon tied in the hair

nodes.label: Denim
nodes.description: The tough cotton twill that jeans are made from, recognisable by its diagonal weave and faded blue colour.

nodes.label: Leather
nodes.description: Animal hide or its synthetic imitation, with a smooth surface that catches highlights sharply.

nodes.label: Wool
nodes.description: Warm fibre spun from sheep fleece, used for knits and heavy coats.

nodes.label: Silk
nodes.description: A fine natural fibre with a soft sheen that drapes and ripples as the wearer moves.

nodes.label: Cotton
nodes.description: The everyday plant fibre most casual clothing is made from, matte and soft.

nodes.label: Linen
nodes.description: A light natural fabric that creases visibly, which is exactly why it reads as summery and relaxed.

nodes.label: Satin
nodes.description: A fabric with a very glossy face that throws bright rolling highlights.

nodes.label: Nylon
nodes.description: A slippery synthetic fabric used for shells and sportswear, often slightly crinkly and reflective.

nodes.label: Tweed
nodes.description: A rough flecked woollen cloth with a visible woven texture, traditional in jackets.

nodes.label: Corduroy
nodes.description: A cotton fabric with soft raised ridges running down it, called wales.

nodes.label: Mesh
nodes.description: An open net-like fabric you can partly see through.

nodes.label: Sequins
nodes.description: Small shiny discs sewn all over a garment so it glitters under any light.

nodes.label: Cashmere
nodes.description: A very fine soft wool that makes light knitwear with a faint halo of fuzz.

nodes.label: Velvet
nodes.description: A dense pile fabric that looks deep and slightly glowing, with colour shifting as it bends.

nodes.label: Lace
nodes.description: A delicate openwork fabric with patterned holes, partly transparent.

nodes.label: Faux fur
nodes.description: A fluffy pile fabric imitating animal fur, which reads as volume and softness.

nodes.label: Suede
nodes.description: Leather brushed to a soft velvety surface that absorbs light instead of shining.

nodes.label: Latex
nodes.description: A rubbery high-shine material that clings to the body and reflects light like glass.

nodes.label: Fleece
nodes.description: A soft fuzzy synthetic fabric used for warm casual layers.

nodes.label: Tulle
nodes.description: A stiff fine net that holds its shape and puffs out, used in skirts and gowns.

nodes.label: Oversized
nodes.description: Clothing cut deliberately several sizes too large, so shoulders drop and sleeves swallow the hands.

nodes.label: Slim fit
nodes.description: Clothing cut close to the body without actually stretching against it.

nodes.label: Boxy
nodes.description: A straight square shape that hangs away from the waist instead of following it.

nodes.label: Cropped
nodes.description: A garment cut short so it ends higher than usual, at the waist or above the ankle.
nodes.negative_fragment: not cut short at the hem

nodes.label: Tailored
nodes.description: Precisely shaped clothing with sharp lines that follow the body's proportions.

nodes.label: Relaxed fit
nodes.description: Clothing with a little extra room, looser than slim but not exaggerated.

nodes.label: Layered
nodes.description: Several garments worn one over another so the edges of each layer show.

nodes.label: Body-hugging
nodes.description: Stretchy clothing that presses right against the body and shows its shape.

nodes.label: Baggy
nodes.description: Clothing so loose that it sags and folds under its own weight.

nodes.label: High-waisted
nodes.description: Bottoms whose waistband sits at or above the natural waist, which lengthens the legs in a photograph.

nodes.label: Low-rise
nodes.description: Bottoms whose waistband sits low on the hips, well below the navel.

nodes.label: Draped
nodes.description: Fabric arranged in soft falling folds rather than cut to a fixed shape.

nodes.label: Structured
nodes.description: Clothing built with enough stiffness to hold its own shape away from the body.

nodes.label: Asymmetric cut
nodes.description: A garment cut deliberately differently on the left and the right, such as one bare shoulder or a slanted hem.

nodes.label: Sheer
nodes.description: Fabric thin enough to see through, so what is underneath partly shows.

nodes.label: Casual
nodes.description: Ordinary comfortable everyday clothing with no dress code behind it.

nodes.label: Streetwear
nodes.description: City street fashion built on hoodies, trainers, caps and oversized shapes.

nodes.label: Office wear
nodes.description: Smart but not ceremonial clothing suitable for a workplace, such as a blazer with trousers.

nodes.label: Formal
nodes.description: Ceremonial dress for weddings, galas and black-tie events.

nodes.label: Sportswear
nodes.description: Clothing made to be exercised in, in technical stretchy fabrics.

nodes.label: Techwear
nodes.description: A dark, technical, utility-driven look built from shell fabrics, straps and many pockets.

nodes.label: Minimal
nodes.description: Plain clothing in few colours with no logos or decoration, where the cut does all the work.

nodes.label: Vintage
nodes.description: Clothing from an earlier decade, or cut to look like it.

nodes.label: Y2K
nodes.description: The early-2000s look: low-rise bottoms, tiny crop tops, shiny fabrics and chunky shoes.

nodes.label: Preppy
nodes.description: A neat collegiate look built on knits, collared shirts, pleated skirts and loafers.

nodes.label: Korean fashion
nodes.description: The contemporary Seoul look: soft neutral colours, oversized layers and a clean, gentle silhouette.

nodes.label: Editorial fashion
nodes.description: Styling made for a fashion magazine shoot, exaggerated and deliberate rather than wearable.
nodes.negative_fragment: not styled as a fashion editorial

nodes.label: Resort wear
nodes.description: Light holiday clothing for hot places: linen, open shirts, sandals and sun hats.

nodes.label: Winter clothing
nodes.description: Heavy warm layers for cold weather: coats, knits, scarves and boots.

nodes.label: Summer clothing
nodes.description: Light thin clothing for hot weather: shorts, thin dresses and bare arms.

nodes.label: Grunge
nodes.description: The scruffy nineties look: oversized flannel, worn denim, band tees and heavy boots.

nodes.label: Bohemian
nodes.description: A loose flowing look with long skirts, prints, layered jewellery and natural fabrics.

nodes.label: Gothic
nodes.description: An all-black look with leather, lace, velvet and heavy boots.

nodes.label: Workwear
nodes.description: Rugged practical clothing built for manual work: canvas, denim, reinforced seams and deep pockets.

nodes.label: Athleisure
nodes.description: Sportswear worn as everyday clothing rather than for actual exercise.

nodes.label: Normcore
nodes.description: Deliberately plain, unremarkable clothing chosen precisely because it draws no attention.

nodes.label: Cottagecore
nodes.description: A soft rural romantic look with floral prints, aprons, puff sleeves and natural fabrics.

nodes.label: Avant-garde
nodes.description: Experimental clothing built around unusual shapes and construction rather than around wearability.

nodes.label: Military style
nodes.description: Clothing borrowed from army uniform: field jackets, camouflage, webbing and olive drab.
